# Introduction

## Clinical and molecular background

Draft the alpha- and beta-thalassaemia background around chromosome haplotypes,
not isolated VCF records. Explain that HBA states vary in copy number, copy order,
hybrid sequence and linked small variants, whereas HBB phenotypes depend on the
primary beta-globin genotype and co-inherited modifiers.

## Original project scope

The original project was a retrospective analysis of thalassaemia genetic testing
at Dubai Genetics Center with five linked aims:

1. characterise the HBA and HBB variant landscape in a diverse referral cohort;
2. investigate whether co-inherited HBA variants modify haematological parameters
   and clinical severity in HBB carriers;
3. assess representation of cohort variants in public genomic databases;
4. characterise a group evaluated using ONT long-read sequencing; and
5. compare findings from conventional Sanger/gap-PCR and ONT testing.

NanoGlobin is the methods component connecting those aims: the cohort defines the
locally relevant genotype states, while the assay model defines which of those
states an ONT primer design can observe.

## Contributions

State contributions only after the final analyses are frozen. Separate cohort data
engineering, retrospective genotype and phenotype results, assay compilation and
observability, primer-aware molecule analysis, candidate chromosome-haplotype
inference, and validation under each declared truth source.
